summary: Unexpected retroactive price-floor applied to a large batch-embedding invoice
description:
Issue summary: Customer BrightVoice AI reports an unexpected increase on a finalized invoice for a multi-hour batch embedding job run on 2026-03-05. The invoice line shows a higher per-embedding unit price (price floor applied retroactively) for hours in which the job was initially billed at the self-serve reserved rate.

Impact: Billing overcharge for one finalized invoice (invoice #BV-20260305) affecting a single dedicated tenant. Customer is requesting an explanation and a credit if the charge is incorrect. Customer reports the delta is ~USD 3,420.

Environment: Dedicated pool (dedicated-nyc-gpu-pool-3) with fallback to hosted when reserved nodes temporarily saturated. Batch embedding controller: batch-runner-v5 (image: runner:2026-02-28).

Steps to reproduce (customer reported):
1) Upload CSV of ~1.2M rows to start a single batch embedding job at 02:10 UTC on 2026-03-05.
2) Job runs across a 7-hour window with autoscaling and a fallback window between 04:00-05:10 UTC when some reserved workers hit capacity and requests routed to hosted fallback.
3) Final invoice shows higher per-embed unit price for entire job, not only the fallback window.

Expected behavior: Only tokens/embeddings routed to hosted fallback should be billed at hosted rates and any reserved-capacity pricing should remain unchanged for hours served by dedicated capacity. Retroactive price floors should not be applied after invoice finalization.

Actual behavior: The billing pipeline applied a price floor rule retroactively to the whole job, increasing unit price for all hours. Customer email thread indicates they saw correct provisional estimate before finalization but were surprised by final invoice.

Logs / evidence attached (referenced): invoice BV-20260305 (PDF), provisional_estimate_BV-20260305.csv, batch-runner logs (s3://bv-embeds/logs/2026-03-05/), billing-postback dump (s3://billing/postbacks/2026-03-05/finalized).
steps_to_reproduce: Start a batch-embed job on a dedicated tenant with autoscaling that triggers hosted fallback
Allow fallback to host for ~1 hour mid-job
Observe postback ordering and final invoice aggregation
logs_snippet: [2026-03-05T04:02:17Z] billing-postback: queued postback id=pb-98a1 for tenant=bv-tenant
[2026-03-05T05:15:02Z] billing-aggregator: applied price_floor=0.000040 to rate_group=embed_standard for tenant=bv-tenant (trigger=price-floor-policy-v2, effective_start=2026-03-05T00:00:00Z)
customer_message: We saw a provisional estimate of ~$1200 but the finalized invoice jumped to ~$4600. We only used hosted fallback for ~1 hour; why would the whole job be marked up? We need a credit or a clear explanation to pass to finance.
comments: Support (Maya): Acknowledged receipt and opened ticket; asked for provisional estimate and invoice PDF (2026-03-10).
Customer (BrightVoice billing contact - Elena Rovira): Uploaded invoice PDF and provisional estimates; requested urgent credit assessment (2026-03-10).
Billing eng (Tomas): Assigned to investigate pricing rule application and postback ordering (2026-03-10).
SRE (Anand Patel): Noted there was a brief control-plane partition at 04:00 UTC that may have affected postback ordering; flagged for triage (2026-03-11).
Billing eng (Tomas): Found runs where price-floor rule evaluation used job-level aggregation instead of per-postback granularity; investigating rollback (2026-03-12).
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: price-floor-policy-v2 incorrectly keyed on job_id aggregation produced an effective_start that backfilled earlier hours when a hosted-fallback event was present.
Postback ordering: billing-postback messages for fallback hours arrived later than dedicated-hour postbacks; aggregator deduplicated and rekeyed resulting in job-level price application.
Config: price-floor-policy-v2 was rolled 2026-02-25 and includes 'job-level' override to prevent undercharging when fallback occurs; test coverage missed multi-postback ordering cases.
SRE note: during 04:00 UTC there was a short control-plane API latency spike (observed in metrics cluster-api: 120s P95) which delayed hosted postbacks by ~30 minutes.
Estimate of incorrect charge: aggregator applied higher unit_price to 100% of job tokens (1.2M rows * 1 embed each) instead of only 124K fallback items; delta =~ $3,420.
Related repo change: commit ab12cd34ef introduced the job-level aggregation accidentally; PR 4823 reverted local test but not deployed to production at the time of job.
next_steps: Hold on finalizing billing credits pending approval from billing manager
Create refund/credit memo draft for BrightVoice (approx USD 3,420) if investigation confirms pipeline fault
Schedule hotfix to change aggregator granularity from 'job' -> 'postback' and add ordering-tolerant merging (track as INT-4382)
Add automated regression test covering delayed-postback ordering to price-floor policy test suite
Notify customer of expected timeline (targeted 2026-03-14 for credit posting)
Coordinate with finance to apply credit and notify customer with invoice adjustment
resolution: Investigation confirmed a bug in billing-aggregator where price-floor policy was keyed at job-level and retroactively applied to full job after receiving a delayed hosted-fallback postback. Billing team to issue a credit memo for the overcharge (USD 3,420). Hotfix scheduled and PR created to rekey aggregation by postback window and add tolerance for out-of-order postbacks. Credit to be posted to customer account by 2026-03-14.
